posts.title: Caching Strategies, Explained Like You're Building It Yourself
posts.description: So, what is a cache? A cache is a small, fast place where you keep copies of things you’ll probably need again soon. Think about your kitchen. Your rice, spices and oil live in the pantry, but the salt you use every day sits right next to the stove. You didn’t move it there because the pantry is broken. You moved it because walking to the pantry ten times a day gets old fast.

posts.title: Timeouts, Retries, and Backoff with Jitter
posts.description: Have you ever wondered when one service calls to another service and you get no response back? its hard to tell of the other side is slow , dead or message got lost. These are 4 techniques how systems cope. I give you what these terms are with analogy and the CS term as well for better understand. Timeouts Analogy: You call a restaurant and it just rings. Eventually you hang up instead of waiting
